definitions.explanation: A sake brewing category where rice is polished to remove at least 40% of the outer grain, producing a lighter, more aromatic flavor.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{蔵|くら}→蔵：13991_kura⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{吟醸|ぎんじょう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{評判|ひょうばん}→評判：03586_hyouban⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧。
examples.english: This brewery's ginjo has a good reputation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{吟醸酒|ぎんじょうしゅ}→吟醸酒：22247_ginjoushu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{華|はな}やか→華やか：06070_hanayaka⟧な⟦{香|かお}り→香り：00189_kaori⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{特徴|とくちょう}→特徴：03456_tokuchou⟧だ。
examples.english: Ginjo sake is characterized by its fruity aroma.

examples.japanese: ⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{誕生日|たんじょうび}→誕生日：02910_tanjoubi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{大吟醸|だいぎんじょう}→大吟醸：25652_daiginjou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{贈|おく}ったら→贈る：09862_okuru⟧、⟦とても→とても：00593_totemo⟧⟦{喜|よろこ}んで→喜ぶ：01169_yorokobu⟧⟦くれた→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。
examples.english: When I gave my father a daiginjo for his birthday, he was very pleased.

notes:
A compound of {吟|ぎん} (to recite carefully, to select) and {醸|じょう} (to brew). The character {吟|ぎん} here implies careful selection and craftsmanship in the brewing process.

Sake is classified by how much the rice grain is polished ({精米歩合|せいまいぶあい}). {吟醸|ぎんじょう} requires polishing to 60% or less (removing 40%+), while ⟦{大吟醸|だいぎんじょう}→大吟醸：25652_daiginjou⟧ requires polishing to 50% or less. More polishing generally produces a cleaner, more delicate flavor.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{吟醸酒|ぎんじょうしゅ}→吟醸酒：22247_ginjoushu⟧: ginjo sake
- ⟦{大吟醸|だいぎんじょう}→大吟醸：25652_daiginjou⟧: daiginjo (ultra-premium, polished to 50%+)
- {純米吟醸|じゅんまいぎんじょう}: junmai ginjo (pure rice ginjo, no added alcohol)
- {吟醸|ぎんじょう}{造|づく}り: ginjo brewing method

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {本醸造|ほんじょうぞう}: honjozo — a less polished category (70% or less), lighter than {純米|じゅんまい} but less aromatic than {吟醸|ぎんじょう}
- {純米|じゅんまい}: junmai — sake made only from rice, water, and koji, without added brewing alcohol
